summary: The Gateway and runner request lanes now bind a session profile's env per thread instead of mirroring it into os.environ, so a concurrent default-profile request keeps the root Gateway endpoint and key.
commit_message: fix(reasoning): keep request lanes on the profile-owned env
commands_run: .venv/bin/python -m ruff check --output-format=concise api/config.py api/gateway_chat.py api/profiles.py api/routes.py tests/test_gateway_runs_model_options_boundary.py

RED evidence on the pre-fix head: git checkout -- api/ && ./scripts/test.sh tests/test_gateway_runs_model_options_boundary.py -q -k named_profile_request_leaves (2 failed: default lane got http://analyst-gw.test)

RED evidence for the config.py half: temporarily restored the os.getenv reads && ./scripts/test.sh tests/test_gateway_runs_model_options_boundary.py -q -k lmstudio_env_key (2 failed: probe sent process-env-key)
risks: Named-profile lanes now resolve the Gateway endpoint/key and the LM Studio probe key from the profile-owned env plus the config snapshot only; a profile that relies on a value defined only in the root .env no longer inherits it (fail-closed), while empty/root-profile requests still read os.environ unchanged. Evidence: the new two-thread pin fails on the pre-fix head for both lanes (default lane read the analyst endpoint/key), and the LM Studio env-key pin fails when only the api/config.py thread-scoped read is reverted (probe sent the process env key). Focused and neighbouring suites passed; full suite through ./scripts/test.sh: 21033 passed, 438 skipped, 2 xfailed, 2 xpassed, 421 subtests passed (no xfail_strict, and no xfail-marked test touches gateway or profile env). No doc changes: routing behaviour for default/root profiles is unchanged. The PR description was not edited (this run writes one branch commit only).
